newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, late rally aids July.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, late rally aids July.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mixed and mostly lower, but a late commercial-driven rally helped prices end well above their intraday lows, traders said.
"We rallied nicely at the close. Commercials bought about a million July (bushels) in the last three minutes," a MGE floor source said.
Traders said the commercial buying in spring wheat was pricing probably tied to Tunisia's recently announced wheat deal. Tunisia bought 125,000 tonnes of Canadian, U.S. or European wheat.

Traders said firm cash basis values for old crop wheat underpinned the May and July contracts. But new crop September spring wheat weakened on continued favorable weather conditions for seeding activity in the northern U.S. Plains.
Losses in spring wheat futures were not nearly as steep as they were in Kansas City or Chicago, and the intermarket MGE/KCBT July spread managed to narrow 11-1/4 cents to close at even money.
MGE spring wheat settled five cents per bushel lower to five cents higher, with July down 3/4 cent at $4.16-1/4. Earlier in the session, July traded as low as $4.09-1/2.
Atwood-Peavey bought one million July bushels, and Linnco bought 1.2 million July. Cargill Investor Services bought 1.3 million September bushels.
